mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates robust labor market conditions, which typically support corporate earnings growth and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are negative in more than 60% of months when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.7% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which often precede economic slowdowns and trigger equity sell-offs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in more than 60% of months when UNRATE exceeds 4.7%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a broad-based economic contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as recession fears intensify.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in more than 60% of months when INDPRO growth is negative and UNRATE rises by more than 0.2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of active monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS rising), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity, producing negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in more than 60% of months during monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising by more than 0.25 percentage points in three months).

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts (HOUST) reflect strong consumer demand for residential construction, which often correlates with broader economic expansion and positive equity market sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are negative in more than 60% of months when HOUST growth exceeds 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When annual inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent price pressures that may prompt aggressive monetary tightening, causing short-term equity market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are positive in more than 60% of months when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising retail sales (RSAFS) and accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates strong consumer demand outpacing supply, which often leads to Fed intervention and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are positive in more than 60% of months when RSAFS growth exceeds 0.5% and CPIAUCSL growth exceeds 0.3% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: During supply shocks (INDPRO declining), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate margins face pressure and economic growth slows.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are positive in more than 60% of months when INDPRO growth is negative.
